correctness.rationale: Breadth-first search over a bijective factorial encoding of S_10, with exactly 15 edge-transposition generators on GP(5,2), computes true shortest distances because FIFO discovers vertices at minimal depth. Left translation makes the Cayley graph vertex transitive, so identity eccentricity equals its diameter. A new, separately written C++ implementation used the Kneser KG(5,2) graph and all 3,628,800 states; its complete distances reproduce exactly 14 shells (largest nonempty index 13), 11,616 distance-13 placements partitioned among seven stated cycle types, and deficit counts (431532,1509516,1382012,299060,6680) for gaps 0..4. Each swap moves two tokens at most one base-graph edge, proving transport lower bound L=ceil(sum distances/2). This is an EXHAUSTIVE FINITE proof for Petersen, not an infinite-family argument.
residual_risks: No formalized proof or external expert attestation; exact finite computation depends on checked separate implementation and standard BFS invariant.

evidence: FUN 2014 gives token-swap algorithms for trees, tree spanners and complete bipartite graphs, not the stated Petersen sphere counts; tree-transposition diameter results assume 9 generating edges forming a tree, whereas Petersen has 15 generating edges and cycles; general search algorithms permit computation but do not imply the numerical output.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General computability or upper bounds do not logically determine diameter 13, antipode patterns or the complete transport-bound gap counts for these generators.
